text:
alex (customer): hey! morning — starting ~07:42 UTC we started seeing intermittent 429s and some billing alerts. Very spiky, not sustained. No app deploys. sample curl: ```curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-77\" -d '{\"input\":\"ping\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat``` headers show `x-rw-scope: api_key` sometimes and `x-rw-scope: ip` other times. body: {\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\",\"message\":\"quota exhausted\"}`

alex (customer): we run behind a managed CDN+egress pool and also have multiple projects under our org. Can this oscillation between scopes be expected?

nina (support): thanks — sorry for the noise. Can you share exact response headers for two samples (one where x-rw-scope=api_key and one with ip)? Also which project id / org should we inspect? If you prefer, DM the key.

alex (customer): sending two sanitized responses inline:
```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 07:43:12 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-rw-limit: 1000
x-rw-remaining: 0
x-rw-reset: 29
x-rw-scope: api_key

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"API key quota exhausted"}```
and
```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 07:43:39 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-rw-limit: 300
x-rw-remaining: 0
x-rw-reset: 12
x-rw-scope: ip

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"IP quota exceeded"}```
Project: proj-99-omega, Org: acme-corp. Billing alerted at 07:45 with UUID bill-556.

liam (eng-sre): quick summary of how enforcement happens here: we maintain multiple quota dimensions (org, project, api_key, ip). Each request is checked against all enabled dimensions; the enforcement point returns the first dimension that is exhausted based on our evaluation order (which can differ slightly by edge cluster). That explains different x-rw-scope values in your examples — different edge nodes or timing hit different buckets first.

liam (eng-sre): dug into logs for proj-99-omega across the edge cluster around those timestamps: some POPs show rapid fanout from your CDN to a small set of egress NATs. Project-level sustained usage is within your committed quota, but short bursts per api_key and per-ip exhausted local buckets. Also noticed you have two API keys in the org used by different services — one key (sk-prod-77) was near its per-key burst limit during the spike while other key had headroom.

alex (customer): hmm that explains it. But why did billing alert? We got charged overage in the same window. We'd expect throttling to prevent overages.

rosemary (billing): hi — billing here. The alert you're seeing was triggered by a momentary consumption spike recorded by the metering pipeline. Throttles are applied at request time, but metering can be slightly ahead/behind due to ingestion lag and some internal buffering. In rare cases a burst of long-running requests (higher token usage) can cause metering to report extra usage before throttles fully stabilize. We'll investigate bill-556 and can submit an adjustment if warranted.

nina (support): couple of actionable items: 1) add short-term mitigations (whitelist stable egress IPs or ask your CDN to use fewer NATs); 2) we'll propose an api_key/project scoping preference for your org so enforcement favors the api_key/project buckets over per-dynamic-ip for your projects; 3) increase per-ip burst for your account if you can't change egress NAT behavior. Which do you want to try first?

alex (customer): prefer scoping change + a temporary per-ip increase. We can't fully stop the CDN from rotating IPs. Can you outline risks?

liam (eng-sre): scoping change risk: moving enforcement to api_key/project reduces protective isolation for shared NAT pools — noisy tenants could affect others if we relax ip enforcement. We'll gate it behind an account review. Concretely we'll: (a) create an internal ticket to prefer api_key/project for proj-99-omega and set per-ip burst from 300 -> 900 for 24h as a canary, (b) whitelist your two CIDRs you DM'ed, (c) instrument extra per-dimension headers for debugging on the canary path.

quota-bot: quota event: proj-99-omega api_key sk-prod-77 reached 100% of burst quota at 07:43:12 UTC (window: 60s)

alex (customer): thanks. Also want guidance on client retries — our frontend retries aggressively which may be making this worse. Any recommended pattern?

liam (eng-sre): recommended: exponential backoff with randomized jitter, cap retries to 3 attempts, and ideally implement request coalescing / batching where possible. For chat/generation, reuse keep-alive connections to reduce NAT churn. Avoid hammering different keys in parallel if they map to same project.

nina (support): i've opened internal escalation INC-2244 and billing case BILL-556. rosemary is on the billing case. We'll proceed with per-ip bump and the scoping preference once we have your signed attestation form for relaxed ip protections.

rosemary (billing): noted — I've provisionally paused auto-invoice for the overage pending investigation; please DM any cost center info. We'll target a resolution within 48 hours.

alex (customer): DMing attestation now and CIDRs. Also— can you make the rate headers more verbose? It would help to know remaining counts per-dimension and a reason code.

liam (eng-sre): agree — we've debated exposing per-dimension headers. Short-term we'll add debug-only headers on canary (x-rw-remaining-api_key, x-rw-remaining-project, x-rw-remaining-ip) and a `x-rw-enforcement-order` for visibility. Product will evaluate full rollout.

nina (support): update 08:10 UTC — per-ip bump applied to proj-99-omega (300->900) and whitelist active. Early telemetry shows 429s down ~85% and billing spike not recurring. We'll keep thread open 24h.

alex (customer): confirmed immediate improvement, thank you. Please include the RCA and exact timestamps of the config change in the postmortem.

nina (support): will do. Closing note: if you want long-term protection, consider a dedicated egress NAT or Redwood Dedicated which avoids shared ip buckets. Happy to set up an intro.
